summary: When Nora finds that something the group believes is wrong, she can now actually record the correction — until now every correction was silently thrown away before it was saved.
details: To retire an outdated fact she has to point at the one she is replacing. She was pointing at it by its internal database id, and her own safety screen — which strips identifiers out of anything a background job produces — destroyed every such answer before it could be saved.
It failed quietly and selectively: findings that merely confirmed or failed to settle a claim went through fine, so the feature looked like it was working. Only corrections were lost.
She now refers to a fact by its position in the short list she was shown, so no identifier is involved and nothing is discarded.
The test proving this works now runs a correction through the same safety screen the live system uses and reads the result back from a store, rather than checking that the code was called.
limitations: The fact tier is switched off in this deployment, so no correction was ever actually lost in production — the defect was latent.
